title: Grateful Dead Live at Greek Theatre, U. Of California on 1968-10-20
lineage: SBD > Rm > DAT > CD > Sonic Solutions > CD

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a short, high‑energy 1968 Greek show highlighted by a soaring Dark Star, fierce Eleven and magical Lovelight.
ai_review.review: The upgraded Miller soundboard tape delivers an almost flawless listening experience – every instrument sits cleanly in the mix with only a faint buzz on Lovelight and a subdued Garcia tone at the start of Dark Star. Musically the performance is electric: Dark Star, The Eleven, Lovelight, St. Stephen and the Elevent→Caution transition are repeatedly singled out as show‑stopping moments, while Schoolgirl suffers a minor balance issue. Overall the set bursts with raw 68 energy and superb interplay among the band.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 detailed reviews uniformly praise both performance and recording; show quality is exceptional and recording is described as crystal‑clear, justifying a near‑5‑star rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crystal‑clear mix with every instrument audible; occasional slight buzz on Lovelight and Garcia's early Dark Star guitar is faint, but overall the tape sounds pristine for a 1968 source.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A concise but high‑octane set that flows effortlessly; notable transitions include Elevent→Caution and a seamless cross‑fade from Lovelight into Dark Star, keeping the momentum relentless.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for hypnotic, flowing guitar tone, especially on Dark Star and Lovelight; his fills are described as “amazing” and “raw energy.”
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is front‑and‑center, “nasty” on Schoolgirl and delivers an extended solo that fans highlight; often noted as “in charge.”
band_member_comments.Bob: Pigpen’s vocals and organ work are called “tip‑top” and “rocking,” adding vital grit to the performance.
